_README: IRON-RULE-2b CLASSIFICATION — the per-talent record behind EDHA_EDITABILITY_AUDIT.md §9.
Re-derived 2026-07-24i against the FULL vocabulary: 43 handler types (31 edha + 12 native)
and 27 event types (10 edha + 17 native). SUPERSEDES the 07-24f pass, which enumerated only
the module's own 31 handlers and produced the void 61/16/118/26 split.
METHOD — this matters, it is why the 07-24f numbers were wrong. Every one of the 218 names then on the list
was classified by READING THE CODE AT ITS CALL SITES, never from the engine's tree-section
header ledgers. The headers describe a talent's MECHANIC accurately but say nothing about
which HANDLER can express it; classifying from headers gave Red '8 of 9 convertible' when
the call sites gave 3. Tooling: call sites extracted with lint-refs pass 7's own comment
stripping (so header ledgers cannot read as call sites), then the body of every function
reached from a name-bearing line was read in full. 218 names, 527 call sites, 132 dispatched
functions, 93 merged context windows.
BUCKETS
1  — an existing handler (edha OR native) expresses it AS-REGISTERED. Pure data move.
1b — an existing handler + ONE new schema field (or one small engine tolerance change).
2  — needs a NEW generic handler. `needs` names which.
3  — genuinely ENGINE-OWNED. Still leaves the allowlist via marker-rule dispatch + a cue
rule + an ENGINE_OWNED: line (audit §9b — bucket 3 is NOT an exit from the ratchet).
THE DIVIDING LINE (verified in the system source, not inferred — see audit §9k):
Native handlers write SELF/OWNER state (`update-actor` Target is `parent` or a fixed
`global` UUID; there is no native 'current user target').
Native EVENTS are likewise OWNER-SCOPED: the system's dispatcher resolves each hook to ONE
document and, for an Actor, iterates `actor.items` — the items of the actor the event
happened TO. A talent never hears about a creature that is not its own actor.
=> native = things that happen to ME; edha = targeting, and watching anyone else.
source: scripts/name-keyed-allowlist.json ∩ register-skills.js call sites (218 names at the 07-24i derivation; 212 now — the six Warrior stances converted 07-24j)

vocabulary.note: The edha event system ALREADY covers engine-detected triggers. What no event system covers — native or edha — is fan-out to N observer actors; both dispatch to exactly one document (`transform` picks it). That, not 'no handler fires on engine events', is why H8 exists.

_splitNote: Recomputed FROM the talents map below, not asserted — the map is the record; any summary that disagrees with it is the thing that is wrong. Verify with scripts/check-2b-classification.js.

handlerDemand._note: Consumers = bucket-2 talents naming the handler in `needs`. Most need two, so these sum past the bucket-2 count. Bucket-1b talents are NOT counted here (they need a field, not a handler).

H8_edha_watch.verdict: SURVIVES — and it is now the LARGEST demand. Justification corrected: not 'no handler fires on engine events' (false) but 'no event system, native or edha, fans out to N observer actors'. See §9k. BUILT 07-24q; the `watch` enum widened 07-24r with `defeat` and `focus-change` (plus payloadTarget / whenTotal / chain), which is schema plus one dispatch call per hook rather than a handler. Still queued and measured in §9o: damage-applied, turn-start, token-move, attack-declared.

H1_edha_def_test.verdict: SURVIVES — the single cleanest win; it is also literally the EDHA_HEROIC_DEFTESTS table made authorable

H3_edha_owner_list.verdict: SURVIVES — larger than the 24 estimated; 6 trees hand-roll the identical capped-list-with-fizzle code. 3 further bucket-1b talents (Risen Servant, Speak with the Fallen, Pinpoint Charge) also read the list, so H3 unblocks 37 in total.

H6_edha_prompt_pick.verdict: BUILT 07-24s (pass J). ⚠ THE 07-24n VERDICT WAS HALF WRONG and is kept here as the correction: "the post-card helpers are already generic and take the talent name as a mere label" is TRUE of the OFFER shape (edhaPostCoordReactionCard branches on no name at all) and FALSE of the PICK shape — edhaPostCalcTestCard, edhaPostBeaconCard, edhaPostReknitCard, edhaPostLifeCleanseCard and edhaPostMutationCard each HARD-CODE a different payload in their click handler, so there was no one function to put a schema over. Built instead as pass H's move: one card+click pair whose click dispatches back through edhaDispatchTestResult, so the payload is the item's own edha-test-success rules and H6 owns no payload vocabulary. Sources `confirm` and `creatures` shipped; `status`, `item` and `effect` did NOT — their payload would have to receive the picked THING rather than an actor and no payload handler takes one, which is why Beacon of Stability, Surgical Precision, Devoted Presence, Reknit Form and Unweaving are still here.

H5_edha_cae_grant.verdict: SURVIVES — but the 07-24f 'single atlas, six heroic paths' is wrong: leyline Black needs it too

H2_edha_zone.verdict: SURVIVES — slightly smaller than the 15 estimated

H7_edha_aura.verdict: SURVIVES — smaller than the 17 estimated; several presumed auras are really H8 watchers

H10_edha_focus.verdict: BUILT 07-24r (pass I). One schema over edhaGainFocus / edhaDrainFocus, which were already generic and had simply never had a handler — the H6 shape. First consumers: Whispered Doubt (drain), Predatory Insight (gain), Siphoned Will (gain, riding Hollow Command as a whenOwnsTalent upgrade rider).

H9_edha_die_step.verdict: BUILT 2026-07-25 (pass 2bT) as `edha-die-step` + the config `edha-die-step-react` (§9m q1, ruled BUILD IT). Consumers read 0 because all of Sovereignty — its 5 bucket-2, both bucket-3 pair talents (re-litigated to full conversions via entry-data couplings) and the 1b Favor rider — converted in the SAME pass that built it.

H4_edha_use_gate.verdict: DOES NOT SURVIVE as its own handler. Reading the call sites, every 'nothing spent' precondition is an inline guard specific to its talent (has a Construct / has a Covenant / target is Weakened / once per scene). The reusable parts are already covered: once-per-scene/turn/round by existing trigger gates, list-count by H3, target-state by H1. Fold in; do not build.

H11_edha_enter_stance.verdict: NEW, found 07-24j during the Warrior conversion — enter a named stance on a combat-timing trigger. Practiced Kata + Vigilant Stance. Tiny; fold into the H5 build.

H3b_edha_owner_counter.verdict: BUILT 2026-07-25 (pass 2bT) as a `mode: counter` on H3 `edha-owner-list` (§9m q6, ruled). Consumers read 0 because all 9 Knowledge bucket-2 talents converted in the SAME pass that built it — the count is legitimately zero, not a measurement gap.

H12_edha_detonate_list.verdict: BUILT 07-24s (pass K). The audit premise was WRONG in the same way H6 was: edhaResolveCharges has a generic SIGNATURE and a name-keyed BODY — it hard-codes i.name === "Pinpoint Charge" (:8511) and edhaOwnsTalent(owner, "Concussive Yield") (:8557). H12 WRAPS those two branches rather than retiring them, so the net ratchet was -2, not -4; Pinpoint Charge and Concussive Yield each still need their own conversion. NOT coupled to the charges ledger — the handler is engine code and reads the flag directly, so it needed none of the legacy-flag-path escape H3ann is blocked on. Also corrected: mergeTerrain MERGES NOTHING (no geometry union exists in the project); it swaps the terrain formula and prints a GM instruction.

H3ann_owner_list_annotate.verdict: NEW 07-24q — NOT a handler: H3's missing `annotate` op (flag the most recent un-flagged entry), plus the legacy-flag-path escape H3 needs to address a ledger it does not itself own. Three consumers of the op shape are already in the engine and the engine NAMES the shape twice ('mirroring Pinpoint Charge', 'the Inevitable-Snare shape'). Blocked behind the same shared-ledger atomicity problem — see §9n pass H.

H13_kneel_widenings.verdict: NEW 07-24q — NOT a handler: two widenings of existing ones, both needed before Kneel can leave. (a) edha-test-rider's whenTargetStatus must accept a comma-list and gain a range gate (Kneel's standing advantage vs compelled/frightened/weakened in Black range); (b) the move-toward-or-nothing preUpdateToken veto must read the house markedBy shape instead of the bespoke `kneelBy` stamp, so a document rule can write it. BUILT 07-25 (2bU): whenTargetStatus comma-list + rangeColor on edha-test-rider; the move veto reads markedBy.compelled (edha-apply-status expire: owner-turn writes it). Kneel converted with it.

H15_summon_sustain.verdict: ✅ BUILT 07-24y — `sustainCap` (a formula) + `replaceOldest` on `edha-summon`, plus `summonTalent` / `summonedAt` stamped at summon time. Forge Construct converted (sustainCap "1", replaceOldest on); Risen Servant's cap-at-tier retired to its document ("@tier", replaceOldest off) but the TALENT stays on the ratchet for its Remains ledger — H3. ⚠ IT WAS NEVER 'TWO FIELDS': a handler executor runs on `use`, i.e. AFTER the system charged the cost, and both gates this replaces refuse PRE-cost ('nothing spent'). So it also needed a generic `preUseItem` veto — the same shape H1/H3/H12/edha-next-test-mod all carry. And `replaceOldest` had NO ORDERING DATA: nothing stamped a creation time, so `.find()` was only ever correct while the cap happened to be 1. Both were invisible in the `needs` column and only showed up by reading the call sites. Summon identity keeps a name-prefix FALLBACK for creatures summoned before the flag existed, compared against the rule's own authored `summonName` — not a literal in engine code.

H23_summoner_rider.verdict: NEW 07-24y — a SUMMONER-SCOPED damage rider, split out of H16 where Tempered Edge had been mis-filed (it is a passive; H16 is arm-and-consume). Two builds, not one: a summoner-walk in `edhaRiderParts` (which today iterates the ROLLER's items, and the roller is the summon) AND a second-damage-instance / ignore-deflect vocabulary that `edha-damage-rider` does not have — it carries ONE bonusFormula joined into the roller's own damage type and cannot read the victim's deflect. Its `summonTalent` prerequisite shipped with H15 on 07-24y. One consumer, one tree: schedule it low unless a second summoner rider appears.

H16_arm_consume.verdict: NEW 07-24v, RESCOPED 07-24y — the arm-on-use / consume-on-next-weapon-hit shape. Withering Touch already implements it by hand (edhaWitherArm + edhaWitherStrike) and Tagging Shot needs it. `edha-on-hit` CANNOT substitute: its dispatcher treats a rule as item-specific iff the talent has a damage formula, so a talent WITH one never fires on a weapon hit and a talent WITHOUT one fires on every hit for ever. Also wants a melee/ranged gate field (edhaAttackKind exists; no schema exposes it). ⚠ 07-24y: TEMPERED EDGE WAS NEVER AN H16 CONSUMER — it is a passive with nothing to arm; re-filed as H23. So this is 2 talents, not 3. Withering Touch converts on H16 alone; Tagging Shot needs H16 PLUS a ruling, because its card promises 'on a hit OR A GRAZE' and it is UNVERIFIED whether a graze reaches applyDamage at all. Two things worth fixing while in there, both independent of the build: Tagging Shot's branch is UNREACHABLE DEAD CODE today (its gate reads the item that rolled damage and its damage.formula is null, so it has never marked a quarry), and the shared heal-cut card picks its source name from the FRACTION (`hcf === 0` prints 'Withering Touch', anything else prints 'Necrotic Grasp') instead of from the `byName` the effect already stores.

H17_target_formula.verdict: NEW 07-24v — a TARGET-scoped formula resolver. Every `@` formula in the project resolves against the OWNER (verified: exactly one `target.getRollData()` exists in 16k lines, in a bespoke Mantle site). Blocks every 'the target's recovery die' talent — Galvanize, Field Medicine, Resuscitation — and the recovery-die PATH itself is still marked unverified in the engine. Two builds, not one: the resolver and the path.

H18_ritual_paid.verdict: NEW 07-24v — an `edha-ritual-paid` EVENT. Blood Price's and Sanguine Reservoir's payloads are both fully expressible today; what does not exist is the TRIGGER. Their names live inside `edhaRitualHpCost`, i.e. inside ANOTHER talent's executor (Dark Investiture / Withering Ray carry the rule), so neither converts alone. Dispatch after the HP deduction the way edhaDispatchOnHit does — knowing no payload type.

H19_slow_turn.verdict: ✅ BUILT 07-24y — `whenSlowTurn` on `edha-test-rider` + a real `edhaIsSlowTurn` predicate; Calculated Patience converted and its `edha.calculatedPatience()` MANUAL toggle retired. The forecast hazard was REAL and confirmed in code: `edhaIsFastTurn` returns false for THREE states (no combat / no combatant / genuinely slow), so `!edhaIsFastTurn` fails OPEN out of combat. `edhaIsSlowTurn` requires a live combatant and treats an UNSET turnSpeed in combat as Slow (the system's getter is `?? TurnSpeed.Slow`, schema initial "slow"). Pinned in tests/engine-helpers.test.js, mutation-checked both ways (naive-negation and unset-is-not-slow each fail 4 cases).

H20_draw_mana.verdict: ✅ EVENT BUILT 07-24y — `edha-draw-mana`, dispatched from the existing Draw Mana hook by `edhaDispatchDrawMana` (NOT GM-gated, unlike the combat-timing dispatcher: Draw Mana fires on the owner's client). Blue and Red converted exactly as forecast — `edha-next-test-mod` {target self, mode advantage, count 1, attr 'int, wil' / 'str, spd'}; both left EDHA_DRAW_MANA, and Red's 'lose your Reaction' rides alongside as an `edha-note` so its wording is editable rather than a string literal in the table. The forecast was RIGHT for once, and the reason is worth keeping: it was made by naming all three legs (executor real, schema fields present including `attr`, event absent) instead of asking whether a handler was registered. The 3 remaining consumers (White / Black / Green) are genuine bucket 2 and unchanged — each is new capability, not a field. ⚠ Beacon of Stability is a TOTAL ORPHAN of one line inside the White branch and Thorn Field / Thorn Hedge of one inside Green; restructuring `edhaDrawMana` kills them silently.

H21_summon_effect.verdict: NEW 07-24v — toggle a named baked effect on your live summon (Siege Form). The classification put this field on `edha-summon`, which is wrong: Siege Form summons nothing and its document has no summon rule. Wants its own small handler (effectName + on/off/toggle) plus a pre-cost gate on 'a live summon of mine carries that effect'. The effect DATA already lives in Forge Construct's bakedEffectsJson, so the two talents' documents are coupled.

H22_wall_cover.verdict: NEW 07-24v — Wall/cover creation. Phantom Barricade's card says it blocks movement and provides cover; NOTHING in the engine does either (no Wall document creation anywhere, and cover is explicitly a table read). Not a field: it needs Wall create from the token footprint, cleanup on HP-0 and on token delete, and a GM relay because players cannot create Walls. Bucket 2/3, not 1b.

H24_reveal.verdict: BUILT 2026-07-25 (pass 2bQ). `edha-reveal` — state facts about a creature as card text (hp / conditions / defenses / lowest-attribute / lowest-defense / below-half, with a hideDefenses subtraction). Its two consumers, Sharp Eye and Vital Diagnosis, converted in the same pass, so this reads 0 and that is correct, not stale. It existed nowhere in any demand column because `needs` recorded only the GATE: Sharp Eye was filed `needs: [H1]` with H1 already built, and the engine's own comment at L4662 said of that row 'what still needs a payload H1 cannot supply'. Reach for it for any scouting/lore-reveal payload rather than hand-rolling another whisper.

H25_damagereact.verdict: BUILT 2026-07-25 (pass 2bQ). edha-damage-react — the Bulwark shape: an ally near you takes damage (or drops to 0) and you are offered a whispered card to spend a resource and intervene. Converted all four White Bulwark reactions at once. It appeared in NO demand column because the four were filed H8+H6 (a watch plus a prompt), and both were built — what was missing was the SPEC vocabulary, which is neither. Adding a fifth reaction of this shape is now authoring, not engine work. Reads 0 consumers because all four converted in the same pass that built it.

Siege Form.why: CORRECTED 07-24v — the field was put on the wrong handler. Siege Form summons NOTHING and its document has no summon rule; it toggles a baked effect on Forge Construct's Construct. Needs H21. Note it is in EDHA_CIV_TAKEOVER, whose dispatch ends in a bare `return false`, so removing the name is step one.

Tempered Edge.why: RE-FILED 07-24y — it was listed under H16 (arm-and-consume) and that is a MIS-ASSIGNMENT its own `why` already disproved: Tempered Edge is a PASSIVE (`activation.type: none`, no cost). Nothing arms it and nothing consumes it, so H16's shape has zero purchase. Its real blockers, verified in code: (1) `edhaRiderParts` walks `actor.items` where actor is the ROLLER — the Construct — while this rider lives on the summoner, so it needs a summoner-walk, not a boolean; (2) its ignore-deflect half is a SECOND damage instance and `edha-damage-rider` has ONE bonusFormula joined into the roller's own damage type, no second-instance and no way to read the victim's deflect. Now tracked as H23. The `summonTalent` prerequisite is DONE (07-24y) — `edhaCivIsConstruct` still name-prefixes, but the flag it should read now exists.
